Region: Originally the central coastal plain; later the far north at Laish (Dan)
History: Dan was Jacob's fifth son, by Rachel's servant Bilhah. Jacob's blessing pictured Dan as a serpent by the roadside (Genesis 49:17). The tribe's first allotment on the coastal plain proved too small and too exposed, so part of the tribe migrated north and captured Laish, renaming it Dan (Judges 18) — the town that became proverbial as Israel's northern border, 'from Dan to Beersheba'. Samson, Israel's most famous judge, was a Danite. Under Jeroboam, Dan became one of the two sites of a golden calf (1 Kings 12:28-30). The tribe was deported with the northern kingdom by Assyria. Dan is the one tribe absent from the sealing list in Revelation 7.
Culture: Danite culture combined coastal farming with the frontier life of a border tribe; its northern city guarded the road into Israel from Syria, and its southern settlements lived among the Philistines.
Religion: Dan shared Israel's worship of the LORD, but its history is marked by two corruptions of it: Micah's shrine with its Levite priest (Judges 17–18) and Jeroboam's golden calf at Dan, which the prophets condemned.
BibleConnection: Dan illustrates both halves of the judges period: a deliverer in Samson and, in the same tribe's story, the spread of idolatry from Micah's household shrine to a royal sanctuary.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 30:6; Genesis 49:16-17; Judges 13:2; Judges 18:1-2; Judges 18:27-29; 1 Kings 12:28-30
RelatedPeople: Dan; Jacob; Samson; Delilah; Manoah, Father of Samson; Aholiab
